info.title: OpenTrust Consumer API
info.description: Read shared compliance posture, resources, subprocessors, machine-readable JSON, and authorized vulnerability findings. Public reads need no key. Protected reads require an organization-issued Consumer key with the documented scope or an authorized session. Vulnerability data is never anonymous. Organization visibility, approval, and customer passkey policies apply. Publishing and internal knowledge operations are documented separately at /api/admin/openapi.json. Existing Management keys remain accepted on these legacy read routes with their original scopes. Data responses use private, no-store caching; lists use data and nextCursor (limit 50, maximum 100). Invalid supplied credentials are rejected.

get.description: Returns only the stored JSON payload, without a data envelope, metadata, HTML, or sign-in redirect. Supports objects, arrays, and JSON scalar values including null. Identical content and permissions are available at /{orgSlug}/machine-readable/{documentSlug}.json, and /machine-readable/{documentSlug}.json for the site-root organization. Public GETs require no credentials. Protected GETs accept a content:read Bearer key or an authorized session. Errors use the standard JSON error envelope. JSON Content-Type, nosniff, CORS, and no-store caching apply.

BearerAuth.description: An active organization-issued consumer key. Required scope is documented in x-api-key-scope; x-api-key-audience identifies the interface. Write permission does not grant read access. Consumer keys must be bound to a verified, administrator-approved company account; approval revocation or account disable invalidates them immediately. Legacy unbound Consumer keys must be reissued. Existing Management keys also retain access to these legacy read paths.

SessionCookie.name: better-auth.session_token
SessionCookie.description: Existing Better Auth sign-in session. Read endpoints only; vulnerability access follows organization policy. When the organization requires customer passkeys, protected reads by consuming users need a WebAuthn-verified session; password-only sessions receive 403 passkey_required. Enroll keys at /account/security. Organization members and scoped Bearer keys retain their existing access.

SecureSessionCookie.name: __Secure-better-auth.session_token
SecureSessionCookie.description: HTTPS session cookie variant. Read endpoints only.
